answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, like a lotus that only opens after it has put down roots. A public atlas of past jobs, ratings and disputes lets others verify that history instead of trusting a fresh name, and one fake identity then costs real capital while gaining nothing. The ripple effect is that creating a thousand throwaway agents becomes a thousand times more expensive, while honest agents keep their stake and reputation.
